subject: Private deployment pricing inquiry and migration buffer options
messages:

Subject: Private deployment pricing inquiry

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this — GreenByte is evaluating private on-prem / VPC deployment for our document ingestion and agent use cases. We need a pricing primer to take to procurement:

- Clarify the licensing model (operator/site license vs per-GPU node).
- How the platform fee is typically amortized for a 12-month pilot vs upfront.
- Support tiers and what response times + SRE credits look like.
- Any migration or onboarding credits you offer for customers moving from another provider.

We have strict compliance requirements (SOC2 + regional data residency) so packaging that includes observability and audit logs is important.

I've attached a short RFP outline (greenbyte_rfp.pdf) with our expected ingest volumes and retention profile. Can we get a simple 2-option pricing scenario (starter predictable vs burst/consumption) and a short memo on migration credit mechanics by EOD Monday?

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform
GreenByte AI

1) Pilot length: you mentioned 12 months — is the goal pilot->production within that window or a true evaluation (we'll show both).
2) Predictability requirement: do you need a hard monthly spend cap or are you open to a blended commit + burst buffer?
3) Compliance add-ons: do you want the audit-log + KMS bundle included in the starter option or as an add-on?

Next steps: David will draft two concrete scenarios and a short note on amortizing the platform fee across the contract term. I'll also attach a working spreadsheet so you can tweak core variables.

Hi Hannah — quick answers inline:

1) Pilot length: 12 months pilot with objective to move to production on month 9 if SLA/ops acceptable.
2) Predictability: procurement will push for a monthly cap. We can consider a blended commit with explicit burst credits, but finance prefers a predictable recurring line item.
3) Compliance: include audit-log + KMS in the starter bundle — that is a must.

On migration credits: we are coming off a provider where we have 6 months of caching and some custom integrations. We're most interested in any one-time migration buffer that offsets the initial dual-run cost. If we commit to a 12-month minimum spend, would Redwood offer a migration buffer or credits against the platform fee?

I can do the 09/11 10:00 PT call. Also attaching our compliance doc for context.

Thanks,
Alex

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing inquiry — draft scenarios and migration buffer mechanics

Alex / team — thanks for the clarity. Below are two concise scenarios and how migration buffers typically work. I kept this intentionally short so procurement has something actionable.

Scenario A — Starter predictable (recommended for procurement clarity):
- Model: Site/operator license + fixed node bundle (e.g., 4 nodes for the pilot).
- Platform fee: amortized monthly across 12 months (line item on invoice).
- Support: Enhanced (24x5, 2-hr critical response SLA, 1x monthly health check).
- Observability/KMS: included in starter bundle.
- Migration buffer: one-time credit equal to 8% of first-year committed spend applied against the platform fee invoice in month 2.

Scenario B — Blended commit + burst credits (recommended if you expect variable token spikes):
- Model: smaller fixed node footprint + consumption for burst (per-GPU/hour or per-inference unit).
- Platform fee: lower monthly amortization + per-usage charges for burst.
- Support: Enhanced with optional Premier on-call add-on for production months.
- Migration buffer: 5% credit on committed portion (applied month 2); burst consumption not eligible for migration credits.

Notes on operator vs node licensing: operator licenses (per-seat with admin access) are separate and often included for SRE/devops staff; node licensing secures capacity per physical/virtual GPU. We recommend operator seats for your SRE team and a 4-node starter for predictable throughput while keeping burst capacity as an option.

SOW / Legal: attached a one-page proposed SOW summary (proposed-sow-draft.pdf) that maps milestones, acceptance criteria and the platform fee amortization schedule. If these scenarios look reasonable we can formalize a MPA + SOW and provide line-item pricing for procurement to review.

Happy to walk through on the call at 10:00 PT.

Best,
David Kim
Sr. Manager, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the quick answers and for joining the call this morning. Quick recap and action items so procurement has a single thread to follow.

Summary:
- We proposed two commercial pathways (Starter predictable vs Blended commit + burst).
- Compliance add-ons (audit logs + KMS) will be part of the starter bundle per your request.
- Migration buffer: we can provide an 8% platform-fee credit on the first-year committed spend for the Starter path or 5% on the committed portion for the Blended path. Credits apply to the platform fee invoice (month 2) and are reflected in the SOW.

Action items (mutual action plan):
1) GreenByte: confirm target pilot commit (monthly $) and primary budget owner by 2026-09-15.
2) Redwood (David/Marissa): produce a line-item commercial memo and draft MPA + SOW by 2026-09-17.
3) Legal/procurement alignment call: schedule once GreenByte confirms budget owner; Redwood will run legal checklist and SOC2 addendum.

If that timeline works I will circulate a calendar invite for the legal/procurement call and attach the draft pricing workbook so your finance team can toy with variables.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this forward.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise GTM — Redwood Inference
